_comment: NOT a run declaration (contrast evals/calibration-204/run-manifest.json): no identities, schedule, image digest or arm order are pinned here. This states the skill-uptake eligibility rule (#203 redesign proposal §2, as amended by the Decision 3 proposal on #203 and ruled by the owner on 2026-10-03) that any future run-manifest for this task must conform to. No live or paid run is authorized by this file (ADR 0005).

fields: selection: opened | not-opened, read from the attempt's retained transcript, same heuristic method #212 and #26 used
outcome: PASS | FAIL on the task's own symmetric endpoint (grader.json's four mandatory criteria via records.derive_status)
eligibility_rule.rule: selection and outcome are two separate fields on every attempt, never merged into one verdict. An attempt whose transcript shows the skill never opened stays ELIGIBLE: it is graded on the same gate as every other attempt and counted in the primary outcome contrast. It is never dropped, excluded, or silently retried.
eligibility_rule.not_opened_threshold_status: NONE, by owner ruling 3c (2026-10-03, https://github.com/cooneycw/skillc/issues/203#issuecomment-5968815648): no threshold. The N arm's opened rate is reported as a measured rate with its count (k/n) and never gates crediting P.
eligibility_rule.p_arm_eligibility: A P attempt is eligible for the value comparison (P vs. B) only if its transcript shows a named skill opened. A P attempt that never opened one is reported with its count as a failed provision, never silently dropped.

arms.approval_ref: operator ruling on #203 decision 4 (2-arm size, ~6-10 attempts, #204's scale)

arms.selection: named by this task's manifest; the task instruction tells the agent to read the named skill(s) before starting
arms.approval_ref: owner rulings 3a (adopt B/N/P) and 3b (P's additional 3-5 calibration attempts), 2026-10-03, https://github.com/cooneycw/skillc/issues/203#issuecomment-5968815648
arms.named_skills_rationale: From the declared subject, cpp-codex @ 85e9b03. flow-auto is the skill that carries CPP's instrument guidance for this hazard: its bundled docs/decisions/0008-instrument-negative-control-bound.md and docs/agents/detector-contracts.md state that a gate needs an input that makes it report the other verdict. flow-check is the skill for running a project's quality gate. Neither SKILL.md names this task or its fixture. Proposed with this change; any calibration declaration restates it for approval.
arms.instruction: Before you start, read the `flow-auto` and `flow-check` skills and follow what applies to this task.

notes: The P arm is a per-run positive control for the opened/not-opened detector: if P registers 'opened' and N registers 'not-opened' in the same run, N's zero is a real zero, not a detector that cannot see a positive.
#26's live attempt (2026-10-03, verdict ok) checked the detector first: treatment detected the named skill, baseline showed no invocation.
